source: Strikingly, though the presence of Sec17 from the start of the incubation blocks the formation of rapid-fusion intermediate with the GST-PX tether (Figure 1E β, red curve)

claim: Rapid-fusion intermediate does accumulate with the GST-PX tether when Sec17 is absent, as Sec17 addition at 30 min triggers fusion.
source: rapid-fusion intermediate does accumulate with the GST-PX tether when Sec17 is absent, as Sec17 addition at 30 min triggers fusion (Figure 1E β, curves a and c).

claim: Inhibition by Sec17 with the GST-PX tether instead of HOPS is only seen when Sec17 is present from the start of the incubation, prior to trans-SNARE assembly.
source: Inhibition by Sec17 with the GST-PX tether instead of HOPS is only seen when Sec17 is present from the start of the incubation, prior to trans-SNARE assembly (Figure 1E, red curve b and green curve d)

claim: Once membranes have undergone tethering and trans-SNARE assembly, Sec17 and Sec18 support zippering-bypass fusion without HOPS.
source: but once membranes have undergone tethering and trans-SNARE assembly, Sec17 and Sec18 support zippering-bypass fusion without HOPS (Figure 1E β, blue and black curves).

claim: Sec17 may inhibit functional trans-SNARE complex assembly.
source: Sec17 may inhibit functional trans-SNARE complex assembly (Wang et al., 2000)
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior work.

claim: Once zippering has begun, Sec17 associates with partially zippered SNAREs to directly promote fusion.
source: but, once zippering has begun, Sec17 associates with partially zippered SNAREs to directly promote fusion (Zick et al., 2015; Harner and Wickner, 2018; Song et al., 2021).

claim: Sec17 can block fusion of reconstituted proteoliposomes without HOPS.
source: Sec17 can block fusion of reconstituted proteoliposomes without HOPS (Mima et al., 2008).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior work.

claim: HOPS engages each of the 4 SNAREs and catalyzes their assembly in a manner which renders fusion resistant to Sec17.
source: HOPS engages each of the 4 SNAREs (Stroupe et al., 2006; Baker et al., 2015; Song et al., 2020) and catalyzes their assembly (Baker et al., 2015; Orr et al., 2017; Jiao et al., 2018; Song et al., 2020) in a manner which renders fusion resistant to Sec17 (Mima et al., 2008; Xu et al., 2010; Song and Wickner, 2019).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to prior work.

claim: Excessive Sec17 blocks the initial stages of fusion but stimulates fusion when added after trans-SNARE assembly.
source: Excessive Sec17 blocks the initial stages of fusion but stimulates fusion when added after trans-SNARE assembly (Zick et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior work.

claim: With the synthetic tether GST-PX, Sec17 which interacts with SNAREs before they assemble into trans-complexes inhibits the subsequent fusion.
source: With the synthetic tether GST-PX, Sec17 which interacts with SNAREs before they assemble into trans-complexes inhibits the subsequent fusion (Song and Wickner, 2019).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior work.

claim: Once fusion intermediates of trans-SNARE complexes have formed, Sec17 and Sec18 will promote zippering-bypass fusion whether tethering is by HOPS or by the synthetic tether GST-PX.
source: We now show that once fusion intermediates of trans-SNARE complexes have formed, Sec17 and Sec18 will promote zippering-bypass fusion whether tethering is by HOPS or by the synthetic tether GST-PX (Figure 1C β and Eβ).
evidence: This is the main conclusion from the current study, supported by data in Figure 1.

claim: Schwartz et al., 2017, found that polyethylene glycol (PEG) and SNARE induced tethering and fusion, arrested by Qc3Δ, could be restored by added Sec17.
source: Schwartz et al., 2017, found that polyethylene glycol (PEG) and SNARE induced tethering and fusion, arrested by Qc3Δ, could be restored by added Sec17.
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior work.

claim: PEG not only tethers, but may enhance SNARE-mediated fusion through promoting dehydration and protein association or, at high levels, induce fusion directly.
source: PEG not only tethers, but may enhance SNARE-mediated fusion (Zick and Wickner, 2013) through promoting dehydration (Lehtonen and Kinnunen, 1995) and protein association (Wälchli et al., 2020) or, at high levels, induce fusion directly (Burgess et al., 1992).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: Dimeric GST-PX only acts as a tether.
source: Dimeric GST-PX only acts as a tether.
evidence: This is an inference based on the properties of GST-PX compared to PEG.

claim: The current findings complement those of Schwartz et al., 2017, and show that a tether and partially zippered SNARE complex allow Sec17/Sec18 induction of fusion.
source: Our findings complement those of Schwartz et al., 2017, and show that a tether and partially zippered SNARE complex allow Sec17/Sec18 induction of fusion.
evidence: This is a conclusion from the current study, relating it to prior work.

claim: HOPS serves both as a tether and as a catalyst to initiate SNARE assembly.
source: HOPS serves both as a tether (Hickey and Wickner, 2010) and as a catalyst to initiate SNARE assembly (Baker et al., 2015)
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: It has been unclear whether HOPS catalyzes the later stages of zippering or is needed for Sec17/Sec18-induced fusion without zippering.
source: but it has been unclear whether it catalyzes the later stages of zippering or is needed for Sec17/Sec18-induced fusion without zippering.
evidence: This identifies a gap in knowledge that the current study addresses.

claim: The engagement of SNAREs by HOPS largely bypasses Sec17 inhibition.
source: The engagement of SNAREs by HOPS (Stroupe et al., 2006; Baker et al., 2015; Song et al., 2020) largely bypasses Sec17 inhibition.
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: Once SNAREs are partially zippered in trans, Sec17 and Sec18 do not need HOPS to support the completion of fusion.
source: Once SNAREs are partially zippered in trans, Sec17 and Sec18 do not need HOPS to support the completion of fusion.
evidence: This is the main conclusion from the current study.

claim: The completion of SNARE zippering is promoted by Sec17.
source: The completion of SNARE zippering is promoted by Sec17 (Song et al., 2021)
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior work.

claim: Sec17 displaces HOPS from SNARE complexes.
source: and Sec17 displaces HOPS from SNARE complexes (Collins et al., 2005; Schwartz et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: The interactions among the SNAREs, Sec17/αSNAP, and Sec18/NSF are seen at a molecular level in the 20s complex, consisting of a 4-SNARE coiled coil anchored to membranes at their C-termini, surrounded by up to 4 Sec17/αSNAP molecules, and all capped at the membrane-distal end by Sec18/NSF.
source: The interactions among the SNAREs, Sec17/αSNAP, and Sec18/NSF are seen at a molecular level in the 20s complex, consisting of a 4-SNARE coiled coil anchored to membranes at their C-termini, surrounded by up to 4Sec17/αSNAP molecules, and all capped at the membrane-distal end by Sec18/NSF (Zhao et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior structural work.

claim: A 'trans-20s' may generally drive fusion, since its elements are common to all exocytic and endocytic trafficking while the tethering complexes of other organelles are varied and often do not have the organelle's SM protein as a tightly bound subunit like Vps33 is in HOPS.
source: A 'trans-20s' (Song et al., 2021; Rizo et al., 2021) may generally drive fusion, since its elements are common to all exocytic and endocytic trafficking while the tethering complexes of other organelles are varied and often do not have the organelle's SM protein as a tightly bound subunit like Vps33 is in HOPS (Baker and Hughson, 2016).
evidence: This is a speculative claim based on the conservation of components and supported by citations.

claim: HOPS only acts for tethering and to catalyze the initial phase of zippering in a Sec17-resistant manner.
source: These findings support the model (Schwartz et al., 2017; Song et al., 2021) that HOPS only acts for tethering and to catalyze the initial phase of zippering in a Sec17-resistant manner.
evidence: This is a conclusion from the current study, supported by data and prior work.

claim: HOPS is specific for fusion at the vacuole/lysosome, but Sec17/αSNAP, Sec18/NSF, and SNAREs are general elements of exocytic and endocytic vesicular trafficking.
source: HOPS is specific for fusion at the vacuole/lysosome, but Sec17/αSNAP, Sec18/NSF, and SNAREs are general elements of exocytic and endocytic vesicular trafficking.
evidence: This is based on established knowledge about the distribution of these proteins.

claim: Sec17 and Sec18 support of zippering-bypass fusion may not be restricted to the vacuole/lysosome, but may contribute to SNARE-mediated fusion at other steps in endocytic and exocytic vesicular trafficking.
source: Our current findings suggest that Sec17 and Sec18 support of zippering-bypass fusion may not be restricted to the vacuole/lysosome, but may contribute to SNARE-mediated fusion at other steps in endocytic and exocytic vesicular trafficking.
evidence: This is a speculative claim based on the findings of the current study.

claim: Testing the hypothesis that Sec17/Sec18 contribute to fusion at other organelles will necessitate the reconstitution of fusion at other organelles with their SNAREs, Rab, Rab-effector tethering complex, and SM protein.
source: Testing this hypothesis will necessitate the reconstitution of fusion at other organelles with their SNAREs, Rab, Rab-effector tethering complex, and SM protein.
evidence: This is a statement about future experimental directions.

claim: Qc3Δ is a labile member of SNARE complexes.
source: Since Qc3Δ is a labile member of SNARE complexes (Song et al., 2021), a fivefold molar excess to the other SNAREs was used in preparing Ypt7/QaQbQc3Δ proteoliposomes.
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior work and explains a methodological choice.

claim: A fivefold molar excess of Qc3Δ to the other SNAREs was used in preparing Ypt7/QaQbQc3Δ proteoliposomes.
source: Since Qc3Δ is a labile member of SNARE complexes (Song et al., 2021), a fivefold molar excess to the other SNAREs was used in preparing Ypt7/QaQbQc3Δ proteoliposomes.
evidence: This describes a methodological detail from the current study.
